The volt-ampere relationship for a diode is given by the diode equation:
$$I = I_0 \left( e^{\frac{V}{\eta V_T}} - 1 \right)$$
where $I$ is the diode current (reverse current here, so $I = -0.9 I_0$), $I_0$ is the reverse saturation current, $V$ is the diode voltage, $\eta = 1$ for Germanium, and $V_T$ is the thermal voltage (approx. $26\text{ mV}$ at room temperature).

Substituting $I = -0.9 I_0$:
$$-0.9 I_0 = I_0 \left( e^{\frac{V}{V_T}} - 1 \right)$$
$$-0.9 = e^{\frac{V}{V_T}} - 1$$
$$e^{\frac{V}{V_T}} = 1 - 0.9 = 0.1$$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:
$$\frac{V}{V_T} = \ln(0.1) \approx -2.3026$$
$$V = V_T \times (-2.3026) = 26\text{ mV} \times (-2.3026) \approx -0.0599\text{ V} \approx -60\text{ mV}$$

**Answer:**
The Diode Voltage is **$-60\text{ mV}$**.
proTip: When current is in the reverse direction, it is negative. A negative voltage confirms the reverse-bias condition.
